title: Correct acceleration calculation
description: Essential: The response must correctly compute the acceleration as 3 m/s² using Newton's second law with friction.

title: Distance for given speed
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the distance traveled to reach 12 m/s as 24 m using appropriate kinematic equations.

title: Velocity at 4 seconds
description: Important: The response must determine the velocity at t=4 s (12 m/s) before analyzing motion after force removal.

title: Deceleration after force removal
description: Important: The response must correctly find the deceleration (-3 m/s²) due to friction alone after force F is removed.

title: Additional displacement calculation
description: Essential: The response must correctly compute the additional distance traveled after force removal as 24 m using kinematic equations with deceleration.

title: Free-body diagram or force analysis
description: Optional: The response includes a clear free-body diagram or explicit force analysis showing normal force, friction, and applied force.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The response maintains consistent units throughout calculations and includes units in final answers.

title: Sign error in friction
description: Pitfall: The response incorrectly uses friction as an aiding force or misapplies its direction in Newton's second law.

title: Kinematic equation misuse
description: Pitfall: The response uses incorrect kinematic equations (e.g., wrong time interval or confusing acceleration values between phases).
